Record Class MazeBounds

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
dev.despical.mazeengine.api.model.MazeBounds
Record Components:
origin - the minimum corner and world identity
width - the positive block count along X
height - the positive block count along Y
depth - the positive block count along Z
public record MazeBounds(MazeLocation origin, int width, int height, int depth) extends Record
Describes an immutable inclusive volume of world blocks.

The origin is the minimum block corner. Each dimension is a block count, so the maximum X coordinate is origin.x() + width - 1; the same rule applies to Y and Z. Maze bounds include the floor and any generated roof.

Construction validates positive dimensions, maximum-coordinate overflow, and a volume representable as a long. It does not require a loaded world or check the world border, build-height limits, or the server's maze-size limits.

  • Constructor Details

    • MazeBounds

      public MazeBounds(MazeLocation origin, int width, int height, int depth)
      Constructs a block volume with representable coordinates and size.

      All dimensions must be positive. Inclusive maximum coordinates are checked with exact arithmetic before the volume can be used for containment queries.

      Parameters:
      origin - the minimum world block corner
      width - the block count along X
      height - the block count along Y
      depth - the block count along Z
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if origin is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if any dimension is nonpositive
      ArithmeticException - if a maximum coordinate or the volume overflows

  • Method Details

    • volume

      public long volume()
      Returns the number of blocks contained in this volume.

      This includes air positions as well as solid blocks. It is the full bounded volume, not the count of structure blocks in a generation plan.

      Returns:
      the product of width, height, and depth

    • contains

      public boolean contains(MazeLocation point)
      Tests whether a world block position lies inside this inclusive volume.

      The point must have the same world UUID and fall within all three coordinate ranges. A position on any minimum or maximum face is included.

      Parameters:
      point - the world block position to test
      Returns:
      true when the world and every coordinate are within the bounds
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if point is null
